D. PRESIDENTIAL OVERSIGHT 
OF ADMINISTRATION
Recent decades have witnessed an intensified debate concerning how 
the president’s powers over administration are most appropriately 
exercised, largely because of a significant series of institutional 
developments within the executive branch itself. Law and practice differ 
profoundly, however, with regard to the president’s engagement with 
administrative decision making in the adjudicatory mode and 
administrative decision making taking the form of rules and regulations.
1. PRESIDENTIAL ENGAGEMENT 
WITH ADJUDICATION
As Chapter 4 explains in more detail, many important agency 
actions—from trial-type hearings at the NLRB or the SEC to immigration 
enforcement proceedings at DHS—do not involve the issuance of regulatory 
rules. Scholars and practitioners generally refer to these non-rulemaking 
decisions as examples of agency “adjudication.” Indeed, the APA treats any 
agency action that is not rulemaking as an adjudication: That is, an
